insight.title: Why You Keep Finding Problems When Things Go Well
insight.subtitle: How your brain invents new issues as soon as you solve the old ones

sections.text: When a neighborhood becomes safer, residents often report more "suspicious" activity. Your brain doesn’t relax when problems disappear; it simply lowers the threshold for what it considers a problem to keep itself busy.
In a famous study, people shown blue dots eventually labeled purple dots as "blue" once the actual blue dots vanished. Your mind is wired to maintain a steady level of concern, regardless of reality.
This explains why a minor typo feels like a disaster on a quiet day. If you don't recognize this pattern, you will spend your life fixing imaginary issues that don’t actually matter.
Try this today: The next time you find a minor flaw today, ask if it actually matters.
High standards are useful, but hunting for ghosts is an expensive use of your attention.

news.title: IMF Lowers China's 2026 Growth Forecast To 4.4% As Iran War Disrupts Global Economy
news.description: The latest projection is slightly below its January estimate of 4.5 percent and well under China’s official five percent growth recorded last year.
news.why: Economic slowdowns could lead to smaller raises and fewer bonus opportunities.

news.title: Disney to eliminate 1,000 jobs
news.description: The Walt Disney Company will cut about 1,000 jobs as new CEO Josh D'Amaro moves to streamline operations. Layoffs will affect marketing, studios, TV, ESPN and tech teams. The move comes as Disney adapts to declining TV revenues, box office pressures and rising competition. It follows earlier cost-cutting efforts, including 7,000 job cuts announced in 2023 to improve financial performance.
news.why: Landing a job in the entertainment industry just became more competitive.

news.title: Adani Energy Commissions 1,000 MW Power Link To Bring More Clean Energy Into Mumbai
news.description: The project, comprising a 30-kilometre (km) overhead line and a 50-km underground corridor, has been designed to operate within the constraints of a densely built urban environment. It also features the world’s first compact HVDC substation.
news.why: Your home will receive more reliable and sustainable electricity.

news.title: To the Moon and Back: How Unison Teams Helped Power NASA’s Historic Artemis II Mission
news.description: Brendon Mee watched the April 1 launch of NASA’s Artemis II, the first crewed mission near the moon since 1972, from a viewing spot about eight miles from Kennedy Space Center.
